assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Generate a NEW simplified medieval pixel-art physical-action reference, not a room terrain scene. Four equal panels in a single horizontal row, crisp restrained enlarged pixel clusters, flat solid charcoal background and minimal stone-grey / wood-brown / iron-grey palette, one brass latch detail. DIRECT OVERHEAD PLAN VIEW, no perspective, no isometric camera. Same camera, same scale, same object and same fixed coordinates inside each panel. Show a short horizontal wall with one gap. ROOM side is ABOVE the horizontal wall; exterior is BELOW. Left jamb and right jamb never move. The hinge is a conspicuous circular iron pin at the LEFT edge of the gap, identical location in every panel. Door is a simple thick wooden leaf viewed edge-on from above, a narrow long rectangle with a few plank joint marks and iron reinforcement, rotating as a rigid object around this left hinge. No tall facade, no ceiling, no barred window, no room textures. The free tip of the door has a small distinctive BRASS SLIDING BOLT permanently fastened to the MOVING WOODEN LEAF, never mounted on the jamb; an iron keeper remains on the RIGHT jamb. Four sequential states left to right: (1) CLOSED: leaf extends horizontally RIGHT from hinge to right jamb; brass bolt visibly extended from free tip into right-jamb keeper. (2) UNLATCHED: leaf exactly same closed position, bolt retracted into its brass housing on leaf, tiny gap before right-jamb keeper. (3) HALF OPEN: leaf rotated COUNTERCLOCKWISE by 45 degrees into upper-right room space, same hinge fixed, free tip ABOVE threshold; entire brass housing and retracted bolt travel with leaf at its free tip. Right-jamb keeper stays empty. (4) FULLY INWARD OPEN: leaf rotated counterclockwise by 90 degrees, extends VERTICALLY UP from same left hinge into room, brass housing/retracted bolt still attached near upper free tip, right-jamb keeper empty. Door length and thickness identical across all panels; no piece of moving leaf extends below the hinge / exterior threshold in panels 3 and 4. Use exactly one brass latch assembly per panel, always on leaf. Sparse original game-concept pixel art, no text, numerals, arrows, motion trails, hands, people, rescue outcomes, water, bloom, smooth rendering or ornamental detail. Prioritize mechanically readable rigid-body continuity. This is concept action reference, not finished sprite sheet.

assets.prompt: Correct ONLY rigid-body dimensional continuity in this four-panel overhead pixel door mechanics reference. Preserve flat overhead camera, left hinge pins, wall jambs, palette, four panels, inward counterclockwise sweep and empty background. The leaf length must be IDENTICAL in all four frames: match the CLOSED leaf length in panels one and two. SHORTEN wooden leaf in panel three by about 25 percent along its diagonal, retaining its same lower-left hinge anchor, 45-degree angle and brass latch at its free upper-right tip. SHORTEN wooden leaf in panel four by about 25 percent, retaining same bottom hinge anchor, vertical-up angle and brass latch at upper free tip. Its upper endpoint should consequently be LOWER than now. Move iron reinforcement bands proportionally. Also make the brass sliding-bolt housing in FIRST panel identical shape and orientation to housing in SECOND panel: long low brass rectangle running along the horizontal wood, two black screws, bolt projects RIGHT out of housing into fixed right keeper only in FIRST panel. Panels two-three-four use same brass housing with retracted bolt, and rotate it rigidly with leaf. Latch always mounted on leaf, keeper only on right jamb. No extra details, people, arrows, words or change of viewpoint. Physical action concept only.
